implementation_notes: The messaging provider is the store: a message sent with DeliveryMode.PERSISTENT (the default) is logged to stable storage when it is sent, so the send returns only once the provider owns it, and a queue or durable subscription retains unacknowledged messages and redelivers them after a consumer restart. Sending inside a transacted session (JMSContext.SESSION_TRANSACTED, JMSContext.commit) makes acceptance atomic across several sends and, in Java EE, composable with database work through JTA. Use it whenever a provider is available; the hand-written spool remains justified when there is no provider, when latency cannot pay a broker round trip, or when the send must be atomic with a database transaction without XA - then an outbox table is the honest answer.
pitfalls: NON_PERSISTENT undoes the guarantee silently and is only safe for messages whose loss is acceptable.
Topics need a durable subscription; a non-durable subscriber's messages are dropped while it is offline.
Sending and then receiving in the same transaction hangs: the message is not visible to the broker before commit (the Java EE tutorial shows the request/reply trap).
The provider's own store must be durable (a file journal on stable storage); an in-memory or non-persistent store gives the API without the guarantee.

variants.name: Transactional outbox table + relay (Debezium Outbox Event Router / poller)
variants.idiom_name: outbox table written in the business transaction + relay to the broker
variants.implementation_notes: Where the send must be atomic with a database commit, the local store is the application's own database: insert the event into an outbox table in the same transaction as the business change and let a relay forward it - Debezium's Outbox Event Router reads the outbox table from the binlog/WAL and produces the broker message, while a plain @Scheduled poller with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED works without CDC. The relay is the forwarder: it retries, keeps the row until the broker acknowledged, and only then deletes or marks it. Choose it over JMS whenever you cannot or will not use XA.
pitfalls: Publishing to the broker inside the business transaction (instead of inserting the row) re-creates the dual write; only the row is transactional.
Relays that delete rows before the broker confirmation, or that do not claim rows atomically, lose messages or double-publish under concurrency.
Without an archive/cleanup policy the outbox table grows without bound, and without an ordering key per aggregate ordering is not preserved.
